course.title: Java 21 and Spring Boot: from a clean checkout to a tested feature
course.description: Learn the actual Craves Java structure, dependency injection, HTTP contracts, transactions, authorization and test evidence. Complete a local-only feature exercise using Academy as the worked example; no production business rule is invented.

lessons.title: Build and navigate a Craves service without guessing the toolchain
lessons.overview: A Java service is a separately built program, not a folder of scripts executed by the browser. Maven reads pom.xml to resolve dependencies, compile Java, run tests and produce an artifact. Spring Boot then starts that artifact and wires its components. In Craves the backend baseline is Java 21 and Spring Boot 3; this training does not upgrade the platform to a new major version. Start in services/auth-service and use AcademyCatalog, AcademyController and AcademyService as a small real vertical slice. In SAP terms, compare a request controller to an entry point and a service to reusable application logic, but do not assume Java shares SAP transaction or transport behavior. A Git commit identifies source; it is not evidence that an Azure runtime has changed.

steps.label: Establish the workspace
steps.detail: Open the repository root and run git status --short and git rev-parse HEAD. Record the exact revision and create a training branch before any edit. Locate services/auth-service/pom.xml, src/main/java, src/main/resources and src/test/java. Keep exercises in this branch; do not edit the running database or production settings to make a local build pass.

steps.label: Verify the executable tools
steps.detail: Run java -version and mvn -version. Both must show the intended Java 21 installation; Maven can use a different JAVA_HOME from the editor. Maven being unavailable is a workstation setup issue, not a reason to rewrite the backend in Node. Read the checked-in pom.xml and Dockerfile for this source revision rather than installing arbitrary latest dependencies.

steps.label: Understand Maven phases
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -f services/auth-service/pom.xml clean verify. Clean removes prior target output, compilation checks all service source, tests execute the configured suites, and verify runs the configured verification lifecycle. A command with -DskipTests is an image-packaging choice, not test evidence. Record executed, failed and skipped totals separately.

steps.label: Trace component construction
steps.detail: AcademyController receives AcademyService, AcademyCatalog and AcademySources through its constructor. AcademyService receives JdbcTemplate, ObjectMapper and the catalog. These are dependencies managed by Spring, not static globals you should initialize inside each HTTP call. For unit tests, instantiate a small component directly; for proxy or configuration behavior, use a Spring-aware test.

steps.label: Trace resources into the artifact
steps.detail: AcademyCatalog loads classpath resources under academy/. The engineering index controls appended lessons and courses. Editing those files in GitHub does not hot-reload a deployed jar: an image containing the new resources must be built and released. If an administrator sees an older catalog, compare the routed response version and running image before blaming browser caching.

steps.label: Read failures at the owning layer
steps.detail: A Java compile error, a failed assertion, a missing dependency download, a database connection failure and an unhealthy Azure revision are different problems. Capture the first meaningful error and the command that produced it. Do not suppress a failing test or change production credentials because a disposable local dependency is missing.

lessons.example: AcademyCoreTest can validate catalog structure without production credentials. AcademyPersistenceTest is enabled only for an explicitly named disposable PostgreSQL database. A green Maven result with persistence tests skipped is not proof of database replay behavior.
lessons.lab: Create a workstation evidence record containing source SHA, Java and Maven versions, the exact clean verify command and test totals. Find the controller method serving the catalog, the constructor loading its resources and the matching core test. In a local training branch only, introduce an invalid question answer index in an unused copy of the curriculum, run verification and observe the intended failure; restore the file and rerun. The exercise is complete only when you can explain why the validator failed and demonstrate a clean diff after restoration. Do not run the persistence suite against any shared database.
lessons.pitfall: A locally generated jar, a successful CI run and a healthy production image are three distinct pieces of evidence. Never substitute one for another.

questions.prompt: The editor uses Java 21 but Maven reports another JDK. What should be corrected first?
questions.explanation: The build must use the intended JDK; the editor configuration alone does not establish Maven's runtime.

questions.prompt: Why do new classpath lesson files not appear immediately after a Git merge?
options: The running image still contains its previously built resources
The questions must all have answer zero
questions.explanation: Classpath resources are packaged in the artifact. Git publication is separate from image deployment.

questions.prompt: What does a skipped PostgreSQL persistence suite establish?
options: No database behavior was exercised by that skipped suite
questions.explanation: Report skipped coverage explicitly and obtain actual execution evidence in the disposable database job.

lessons.title: Implement the request contract and authorization boundary first
lessons.overview: An HTTP endpoint is a contract between a caller and a service. Its path and method describe the operation, its request DTO constrains data, its verified principal identifies the actor, and its response communicates a result without leaking internals. AcademyController provides a real example: the controller is conditional on the Academy feature flag, catalog reads require an internal administrator, plan changes require PLATFORM_ADMIN, and reports require a platform or audit administrator. A frontend button is not a security control. A support administrator being allowed to study a course does not mean that administrator may execute every operational action explained in the course.

steps.label: Locate the exact route
steps.detail: Read the class-level /api/v1/admin/academy mapping together with the method annotation. For example, /catalog is a GET and /attempts is a POST. Do not infer a public URL directly from the controller because APIM and the web BFF compose their own paths. Write the browser, gateway and Java paths as three separate columns.

steps.label: Identify the actor
steps.detail: requireAdmin obtains CurrentUser from Spring Authentication. The identity for submit comes from that verified user; it is not a request field. A proposed DTO must never add identityId merely to make tests convenient. Use two synthetic principals in tests to prove that request data cannot select another learner's records.

steps.label: Read validation precisely
steps.detail: The Attempt record constrains requestId, courseId, lessonId, version and answer count. Bean validation catches malformed shape, but AcademyService still checks the actual current course version, lesson existence and valid option range. Both layers matter. Do not claim @Valid proves ownership, authorization or allowed state transitions.

steps.label: Choose response semantics
steps.detail: The service distinguishes stale or conflicting requests, invalid answers and practice throttling. Preserve these distinctions in an API contract. Unexpected database or dependency failures must not become fabricated success. Review the existing BFF's allowed status mapping before changing a backend error, because the UI may intentionally hide internal details.

steps.label: Test real entry points
steps.detail: Direct calls to requireAdmin test the helper but do not prove filter ordering, a Spring route mapping or a gateway policy. Add controller or HTTP integration coverage for any changed route and retain existing helper tests. Exercise anonymous, customer, chef, supported administrator and wrong administrative permission cases.

steps.label: Preserve private responses
steps.detail: Academy responses use no-store and noindex controls. Keep private values out of URLs, exception messages and diagnostic body logging. The public repository already exposes source-controlled lesson answers, so the quiz is a learning check rather than a confidential certification examination. Do not publish internal plans or learner data alongside source.

lessons.example: A local-only bookmarked lesson command would accept the lesson identifier and a request receipt, derive the owner from Authentication, validate that the lesson exists and return the owner's result. It would not accept an arbitrary owner or expose an unfiltered table. This is an exercise design, not an already implemented Craves endpoint.
lessons.lab: Write a contract worksheet for that local-only bookmark exercise: route, DTO fields, actor source, allowed role, success status, unknown lesson, malformed request, wrong principal, duplicate receipt and cache headers. Map each row to a test at the correct layer. Review AcademyController and AcademyCoreTest side by side and explicitly mark which required tests are helper tests versus actual HTTP tests. Do not implement or deploy a new production endpoint from this worksheet without the relevant architecture and functional-spec approval.
lessons.pitfall: Do not confuse authentication, authorization, validation and ownership. A request may be authenticated and well formed while still being forbidden.

questions.prompt: Where must the learner identity for a protected mutation come from?
questions.explanation: The authenticated principal binds a request to its actor; client-selected identities cannot replace that boundary.

questions.prompt: Does a unit test of requireAdmin prove that APIM routes and Spring filters enforce the same policy?
options: No; route and filter behavior require additional integration evidence
questions.explanation: Helper tests and routed HTTP tests exercise different layers and must not be conflated.

questions.prompt: An internal administrator can read a course about refunds. What follows?
options: Only learning access is established; operational authorization is separate
The user becomes a financial approver
questions.explanation: Course access does not grant permissions to perform the operations taught.

lessons.title: Prove transactions and idempotency with the Academy worked example
lessons.overview: A transaction groups local database changes so that they commit together or roll back together. Idempotency makes an equivalent repeated command return one durable outcome instead of repeating its effect. They solve related but different problems. AcademyService.submit demonstrates both: it verifies the content version, computes a request fingerprint, locks the learner row, checks prior receipts, grades server-side, updates progress, inserts uniquely keyed XP awards and stores the response. Read the actual implementation before adapting the pattern. A JVM lock alone cannot coordinate two service instances, and a network timeout does not prove the first command failed.

steps.label: Define the invariant
steps.detail: For a learner and content version, each passed lesson contributes at most one lesson reward and each completed course at most one course bonus. A given request receipt cannot be reused with different answers. State this in plain language before choosing tables or synchronization code.

steps.label: Follow transaction entry
steps.detail: submit is annotated @Transactional. In a Spring application, the caller must reach the managed bean through the applicable transaction proxy. AcademyPersistenceTest creates the service directly and therefore wraps calls in TransactionTemplate. Copying the direct construction without that transaction wrapper would not reproduce the production transaction boundary.

steps.label: Follow the database lock
steps.detail: learner(id,true) uses SELECT FOR UPDATE after ensuring the learner row exists. This serializes this learner's writes in PostgreSQL. It does not globally serialize all customers or all Craves orders. Draw the exact scope of the lock and avoid calling slow external providers while holding a database lock in a new design.

steps.label: Bind the receipt to content
steps.detail: The request fingerprint includes version, course, lesson and answers. A matching stored receipt returns its recorded result; a changed fingerprint yields a conflict. Return the previously recorded result for an uncertain retry rather than inventing a second receipt simply to bypass a conflict.

steps.label: Separate history from rewards
steps.detail: Attempts are short-lived evidence, while the XP ledger has durable uniqueness for rewards. Removing old attempt receipts must not make rewards available again. The progress query is content-version scoped, while XP sums the retained ledger. A new curriculum version can require new assessments without deleting earned historical XP.

steps.label: Test the failure windows
steps.detail: Use the dedicated disposable database suite for concurrent identical receipts, changed answers under one receipt, replay after retention and separate learners. Add an explicit rollback test around a deliberately raised exception in a local exercise and inspect all related table counts. Do not infer atomicity from a single successful return value.

lessons.example: Four concurrent submissions with the same actor and receipt should produce one attempt row and one lesson award. Each response may report the stored earnedXp value from the original result; summing response values is not the ledger balance. The persistence test checks stored state rather than counting client notifications.
lessons.lab: Run the existing AcademyPersistenceTest only against craves_academy_ci. Explain the transaction wrapper and predict the attempt and XP row counts before running the concurrent test. In a separate local test, reuse the receipt with changed answers and assert conflict with unchanged ledger totals. Then examine retention and demonstrate that old attempts disappear without changing XP. Save expected, actual, pass/fail, source SHA and test report location. A test database name alone is not permission to use a shared host; it must be a disposable local or CI instance.
lessons.pitfall: Do not remove unique constraints, shorten the transaction or replay uncertain writes merely to make a failing concurrency test turn green.

questions.prompt: Why does AcademyPersistenceTest wrap direct service calls in TransactionTemplate?
options: Direct construction does not activate Spring's transactional proxy
questions.explanation: The test must establish a real transaction explicitly when it does not call a Spring-managed proxied bean.

questions.prompt: Repeated stored responses show earnedXp=40. How is actual XP verified?
questions.explanation: Idempotent responses repeat the original result; they do not represent additional awards.

questions.prompt: What should happen when one receipt is reused with different answers?
options: Accept the most recent answer silently
Return a conflict without another reward
questions.explanation: A receipt is bound to its payload fingerprint and cannot be repurposed.

lessons.title: Capstone: deliver an independently reviewable Java change
lessons.overview: The goal of training is not to memorize annotations; it is to deliver a change another engineer can understand, reproduce, review and recover. This capstone uses a local-only Academy exercise because it avoids inventing prices, commissions, food rules or provider contracts. First prove the unchanged baseline. Then write a small approved-style contract, implement one coherent change on a training branch, test its negative and concurrency behavior, and produce a release packet. Completion requires an actual reviewed diff and evidence, not merely clicking through this lesson. The exercise does not grant access to the production environment or claim that the hypothetical capability already exists.

steps.label: Write the decision record
steps.detail: State the problem, owning module, actor, durable fact, API shape, data sensitivity and non-goals. For the hypothetical bookmark feature, explicitly exclude changes to roles, payments, delivery selection and learner grading. List the relevant HLD and functional-spec sections that would require owner approval before a production implementation.

steps.label: Make a complete file plan
steps.detail: Identify the exact existing Academy package and test directory. List every proposed new or changed file and its responsibility. If persistence is needed, choose the next unused migration version only after inspecting all existing migrations on the development branch. Never overwrite an applied migration or assume the next number from a course snapshot.

steps.label: Build from the owner outward
steps.detail: Implement authoritative Java behavior and tests before a UI form. Keep DTOs narrow, SQL parameterized, ownership enforced and transactions explicit. Reuse established service patterns where their guarantees match this feature. Do not add a new Node backend, database server, authentication bypass or external AI dependency to solve a small internal feature.

steps.label: Demonstrate adversarial cases
steps.detail: Provide test evidence for a valid actor, an unauthorized actor, another owner, malformed input, replay and a failure after an intermediate local write. Explain any uncovered HTTP or database behavior. Tests that assert only that a method did not throw are insufficient where durable state and privacy are the risk.

steps.label: Inspect the complete diff
steps.detail: Run git diff --check and review git diff --stat plus the full changed files. Confirm that only planned paths changed and that no secret, real user fixture or generated dependency directory was added. Test names should explain the protected invariant so future editors understand why a failure matters.

steps.label: Prepare release and recovery evidence
steps.detail: Write setup commands, required non-secret configuration names, verified test totals, image/source linkage, smoke cases and rollback behavior. Keep production values in existing secret stores. A production implementation must pass the established release process; a local capstone must stop before resource provisioning, provider calls or shared-database changes.

lessons.example: A reviewer should be able to start from the requirement, locate the DTO and service, run the tests and explain what happens if two requests arrive together. If the only evidence is a working button screenshot, the vertical slice has not been demonstrated.
lessons.lab: Submit a local training pull request or patch containing the requirement worksheet, complete implementation files, README and automated tests for the hypothetical feature. A peer must reproduce the baseline, run your tests, explain the authorization boundary and identify the rollback point without asking where files belong. Assess ownership, security, correctness, replay behavior, test reproducibility and recovery separately. Do not merge the exercise into production merely to earn training completion; the Academy quiz records knowledge checks, not peer approval of your code.
lessons.pitfall: A large generated patch is not automatically enterprise-grade. A small, source-traceable change with independent tests and a credible rollback is stronger evidence.

questions.prompt: Which artifact best demonstrates practical feature-building competence?
options: A reproduced, reviewed implementation with negative tests and recovery evidence
questions.explanation: Practical competence requires an independently reproducible change, not only a quiz or visual result.

questions.prompt: How should the next migration version be chosen?
options: Inspect the current branch for the next unused version
questions.explanation: Migration numbering must follow the actual current repository and applied-history constraints.

questions.prompt: Does finishing this capstone authorize production deployment?
options: Yes, if the patch is small
No; normal approval and release controls still apply
questions.explanation: Training and production authorization are independent.
